text:
carol_prod: Hey team, we're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx responses from the auth path (`POST /token/validate`) for EU region. Errors look like kvcloud token-store failures, upstream returns 502/connection resets. Rate limiter is spiking and causing downstream 429s for some clients. Noticing ~10% error rate for eu-west in the last 3m. Paging on-call.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED (P2) — Managed cache provider degradation: kvcloud (eu-west). Pager sent to @sre-oncall. Incident channel: #inc-1815554321. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-provider-degradation.

sre-oncall: Oncall here, joining. Carol — can you paste representative logs (auth service + rate-limiter) and confirm which routes/customers are impacted? I'll pull up dashboards and start mitigation.

carol_prod: Logs snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T09:05:12Z] auth-service[e4f]: ERROR token-validate kvcache:get failed: EOF
[2026-03-15T09:05:12Z] rate-limiter[e4f]: upstream error from kvcloud: 502 Bad Gateway
[2026-03-15T09:05:13Z] auth-service[e4f]: fallback to db fetch failed? db ok but higher latency
stack: at org.redwood.auth.TokenStore.get(TokenStore.java:112)
```

alice_platform: Confirming — our telemetry shows Cache hit-rate dropped from 95% -> 30% and kvcloud status page shows a partial region outage: https://status.kvcloud.example.com/incidents/eu-west-token-store. Impact: auth token validation and our rate limiter (which uses kvcache) experience high error/miss rates. This leads to client-facing 5xx and automated refresh storms.

ben_support: Support is getting customer reports, primarily EU customers. Top impacted tenant: AcmeCorp (CS case #7654). Queue is filling. Recommending we escalate to 3rd-party support and notify customers via status page.

sre-oncall: Triage decision: do a short-term bypass of kvcache for token validation to fallback to DB (keeps auth correct but increases DB load). Also add protective throttle to token refresh endpoints to prevent stampede. I'll run the feature-flag flip now. Runbook section: Fallback->DB (step 2).

sre-oncall: Executing flag flip: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://flags.internal/api/flags/kvcache_bypass \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"environments":["eu-west"],"enabled":true}'
# response: {"status":"ok","changed":true}
```

ops_dave: DB prep done — increased auth DB pool and warmed replicas for eu cluster: set AUTH_DB_MAX_CONN=500 on auth-service-eu, rolled config, verified replica lag < 5s.

alice_platform: After the flag, error rate dropped: 5xx from ~10% -> ~0.5% within 90s. Latency is up (p50 +120ms) but service is functional. Added temporary token-refresh throttle: limit refresh endpoints to 20r/s across EU to avoid DB overload. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/auth-eu?from=now-30m.

ben_support: Notifying customers on status page now with the following note: "We detected degraded behavior in our token cache provider (kvcloud) impacting auth for EU. We have implemented a safe fallback to our primary DB which restores functionality; some requests may see slightly higher latency. We're monitoring and will update." Sending proactive emails to top impacted accounts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded to P3 after mitigations. On-call handoff scheduled in 2h. Owner requested for postmortem: @alice_platform suggested. Vendor ticket submitted to KVCloud (ticket #KV-9821).

alice_platform: I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with KVCloud support. Action items: 1) collect full timeline and traces, 2) keep kvcache_bypass flag on for at least one maintenance window, 3) plan gradual revert after vendor confirms stability and we validate cache warm-up, 4) add automated throttle to token-refresh clients as permanent guard. I'll open a follow-up doc and assign RCA tasks.

carol_prod: Notes for timeline: 09:04 first spike, 09:06 pager, 09:08 flag flip, 09:10 errors drop. Will attach logs/traces to the incident doc. After vendor confirms healthy we'll schedule revert during low traffic and run local warmup.

sre-oncall: Leaving notes here for next shift: avoid reverting flag until KVCloud provides 24h stable window and we validated cache hit-rate > 90%. If DB starts to show sustained high CPU or connection saturation, revert throttle and coordinate with infra to scale DB further.

incident-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED — please update the incident channel with any vendor updates. Postmortem owner: alice_platform. Link to incident timeline: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1815554321."
